title: PCA of Probability Measures: Sparse and Dense Sampling Regimes
topic: General Machine Learning->Unsupervised and Semi-supervised Learning
claim: In the dense regime, error decays with the number of measures at a rate consistent with theory across all embeddings.
layout: 2 side-by-side log-log plots, shared x-axis, legends with fitted slopes
description: Two side-by-side log-log line plots share the x-axis n, running from 10^1 to 10^3. Panel (a) shows the covariance estimation error E||Σ̂−Σ||_HS on the y-axis. abstract: A common approach to perform PCA on probability measures is to embed them into a Hilbert space where standard functional PCA techniques apply. While convergence rates for estimating the embedding of a single measure from $m$ samples are well understood, the literature has not addressed the setting involving multiple measures. In this paper, we study PCA in a double asymptotic regime where $n$ probability measures are observed, each through $m$ samples. We derive convergence rates of the form $n^{-1/2} + m^{-Î±}$ for the empirical covariance operator and the PCA excess risk, where $Î±>0$ depends on the chosen embedding. This characterizes the relationship between the number $n$ of measures and the number $m$ of samples per measure, revealing a sparse (small $m$) to dense (large $m$) transition in the convergence behavior. Moreover, we prove that the dense-regime rate is minimax optimal for the empirical covariance error. Our numerical experiments validate these theoretical rates and demonstrate that appropriate subsampling preserves PCA accuracy while reducing computational cost.
